explanations.answer: The land is departing from the LORD
explanations.explanation: That's the reason He gives, friend. He says, "…because this land is flagrantly prostituting itself by departing from the LORD." (Hosea 1:2) So the reason is about the land, not about Hosea. I think that's worth a slow read, because it's a heavy way to start a book.

explanations.answer: Hosea has been hiding from the LORD
explanations.explanation: Nope, friend, nobody here is playing hide and seek. The text never says Hosea was hiding from anything. The LORD says the reason is that "this land is flagrantly prostituting itself by departing from the LORD." (Hosea 1:2) The land is the one walking away, and Hosea is the one being spoken to.

explanations.answer: The kings have stopped praying to the LORD
explanations.explanation: I get why you'd pick it, since the verse before this one mentions all those kings. But the LORD never says anything about praying or about the kings here. He says "this land is flagrantly prostituting itself by departing from the LORD." (Hosea 1:2) Stick to what He actually says, friend, because that's the reason on the table.

It's a fair guess, friend. That's a big ask, and most of us would have questions ready. But the text doesn't show Hosea pushing back at all. It says, "So Hosea went and married Gomer daughter of Diblaim…" (Hosea 1:3) No refusing, no arguing.

That's right, friend. No pushing back, no refusing. The text says, "So Hosea went and married Gomer daughter of Diblaim…" (Hosea 1:3) It doesn't give us a single word of argument from him, and I won't make one up either.

That's it, baker. The LORD says, "…I will put an end to the kingdom of Israel." (Hosea 1:4) Israel was the northern kingdom, and Jeroboam was its king when this word came. Bloodshed on the house of Jehu, and an end to the kingdom. Both are in the same verse.

Close neighbor, wrong address, friend. Judah was the other kingdom, the southern one. The LORD says, "…I will put an end to the kingdom of Israel." (Hosea 1:4) And hang onto Judah, because the LORD has something different to say about it a few verses later.

Moab is a whole other nation, friend, so that one came from way out in left field. The LORD is talking about God's own people here. He says, "…I will put an end to the kingdom of Israel." (Hosea 1:4) This word is about Israel, not a country next door.

Yes, baker! The LORD says, "And on that day I will break the bow of Israel in the Valley of Jezreel." (Hosea 1:5) A bow is a weapon, so I think breaking it points to Israel's strength being broken. That's my guess, though, because the verse itself just says what He will break.

Good thinking, friend, since Samaria was Israel's capital city. But the LORD never mentions its walls here. He says, "I will break the bow of Israel in the Valley of Jezreel." (Hosea 1:5) It's a bow He breaks, not a wall.

That one sounds official, friend, but it's not in this passage. The LORD doesn't say anything about altars here. He says, "I will break the bow of Israel in the Valley of Jezreel." (Hosea 1:5) A bow, in that valley, on that day.

I see why you'd think so, friend. The LORD just said He'd have no more compassion on Israel, so it sounds like a package deal. But it's not. He says, "Yet I will have compassion on the house of Judah, and I will save them…" (Hosea 1:7) That little word "Yet" turns the whole thing around.

You caught it, baker. The LORD says, "Yet I will have compassion on the house of Judah, and I will save them…" (Hosea 1:7) That word "Yet" is doing a lot of work. Israel hears one word, and Judah hears a different one.

That's the one, baker. He says He'll save them "…not by bow or sword or war, not by horses and cavalry, but by the LORD their God." (Hosea 1:7) Notice how many things He lists that won't do it. Then He names the one that will.

explanations.answer: By bow and sword in battle
explanations.explanation: That's the exact thing He rules out, friend. He says He'll save them "…not by bow or sword or war, not by horses and cavalry, but by the LORD their God." (Hosea 1:7) Bows and swords are on the "not" list. The LORD their God is the answer.

Egypt is a good guess for a sneaky backup plan, friend, but it never comes up here. The LORD says He'll save them "…not by bow or sword or war, not by horses and cavalry, but by the LORD their God." (Hosea 1:7) No treaties and no armies. He's the one who saves them.
Right, baker. The LORD says, "Name him Lo-ammi, for you are not My people, and I am not your God." (Hosea 1:9) Those are His exact words. It's a hard sentence, and I won't dress it up.

I know it's a lot to take in, friend, so doubting it makes sense. But it's really what He says. "Name him Lo-ammi, for you are not My people, and I am not your God." (Hosea 1:9) The quote on the card matches the verse word for word.
